title: Eleven tree walks in panes.rs, three pairs of which can merge
body:
`arrange_node`, `split_leaf`, `split_path`, `swap_leaves`, `split_beside`, `remove_leaf`, `first_leaf`, `sibling_leaf`, `find_boundary`, `node_area` and `node_at` each walk the tree in `panes.rs`, and `save.rs` adds `saved_node` and `node`.

- `split_leaf` is `split_beside` with side `Right` or `Below`, and `add_transient` can call `split_beside`. Its root-wrapping fallback cannot fire while `focused` is always a leaf.
- `node_area` and `node_at` walk the same path and are called as a pair at two sites. One `split_at(&mut root, area, path) -> Option<(&mut f32, CellRect)>` replaces both.
- `sibling_leaf` runs just before `remove_leaf` in `Layout::remove` to find the heir. `remove_leaf` can return the heir as it promotes the sibling.

Smaller seams in the same file: `Layout::new` repeats the literal of `Layout::restore` and hard-codes a pane named `"terminal"` that both callers in `workspace.rs` patch; `client_rect(&self, pane)` never uses `self`; `bar_row` re-derives `inner()` and has one caller; `arrange` and `inner` are `pub` with no outside caller. About 50 lines go.
